headline: DepEd Estimates ₱7.783 Billion Needed to Repair Schools Hit by Habagat and Cyclones
seoTitle: DepEd: ₱7.783B Needed for Damaged Schools | FMB News
seoDescription: DepEd estimated ₱7.783 billion for cleanup, repairs and reconstruction after monsoon rains and cyclones damaged more than 11,000 classrooms nationwide.
deck: The estimate covers immediate cleanup, minor and major repairs, and reconstruction of heavily damaged school sites.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Education estimated that rehabilitation of schools damaged by floods, the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones would require about ₱7.783 billion.
More than 11,000 classrooms were affected nationwide.

sections.heading: Where the money would go
paragraphs: DepEd's estimate included about ₱65.036 million for cleanup and clearing at 2,243 schools, ₱319.97 million for minor repairs at 1,487 schools, ₱1.194 billion for major repairs at 669 schools and about ₱5.62 billion to reconstruct 490 heavily damaged school sites.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Damaged classrooms disrupt learning well after floodwaters recede, making school rehabilitation a major part of disaster recovery rather than a short-term cleanup task.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The final pace of repairs will depend on funding releases, damage validation, procurement and the ability to keep learning going while facilities are restored.
